verdicts.reason: A: the legal fine print opens the banner on the far left, as large as the subhead, so it is the first thing read. The logo is a speck, and the 'Longest Day Sale' ribbon is shrunk to illegibility and collides with the phone. The headline in the centre and the clear CTA pill on the right do keep the core message to action order. B: the CTA is a tiny pill buried at the far left beneath the logo, so the action comes before the message. The legal copy is jammed under the headline at almost subhead size, making the centre column a cramped stack of text. The ribbon is again tiny and the phone is crushed into the right edge, so B's hierarchy is worse.
